evidence_class: Mixed and labelled per claim in data.evidence_classes. Native execution on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 with retained hashes and sanitized excerpts (template class native_proven) for the per-run exit codes, seconds, outcomes, controls and the oracle verdict; independent observation of platform records (read-only gh REST GET calls on 2026-10-03) for the job, step, artifact and macOS-queue records; local integration for the reproductions on CPython 3.12.3 and 3.13.16; source review for unittest-parallel, CPython and GitHub documentation at pinned commits. Not an upstream test, not a synthetic fixture and not acceptance of any change.
kind_basis: compatibility_attempt as docs/evidence.md defines it ('A new release was installed or executed with a recorded success/failure'; 'Failed attempts remain visible and cannot certify the active runtime'): unittest-parallel 1.8.6 was installed from a hash lock and executed against this repository's whole suite on hosted runners, and failed.
claim: Hosted run 37109532421 (workflow 'Suite parallelism trial (draft pull request only)', the pull_request run of draft pull request #646 at head 1e4bb5ab7c79faa83e4cd8d04cf8dc6d33c7b0de, run_attempt 1) executed the preregistered whole-suite comparison on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 (runner image 20260927.320.1, CPython 3.12.3, 4 CPUs, X64). The serial arm S (python3 -m unittest -v --durations 25) ran 9,823 tests, OK (skipped=967), exit 0, in all three runs, with test-step seconds 1,688, 1,659, 1,186. All nine unittest-parallel 1.8.6 runs exited 1 with TypeError: cannot pickle '_contextvars.Context' object, raised from pool.map at unittest_parallel/main.py line 160, and printed no 'Ran N tests' line: L4 (-j 4 --level module) 649, 438, 459 s, L4F (L4 plus --disable-process-pooling) 539, 692, 710 s, L4C (-j 4 --level class) 667, 659, 704 s. In every module-level run 199 inventory ids never ran, and 82 in every class-level run, all in tests/test_adaptive_paper_fees.py, tests/test_adaptive_paper_transport.py and tests/test_adoption_version_probes.py. The frozen oracle (compare.py) marked all nine runs ineligible and gave ubuntu-24.04 the outcome reject (no parallel arm is eligible); every control and crash control passed, the base-to-trial id mapping was ok and every checkout stayed clean. The coordinator cancelled the run at 2026-10-03T09:12:40Z, 15 s after the last Linux arm job finished; none of the 20 macos-15 jobs had received a runner, so macos-15 has no verdict and nothing was measured on macOS. Local reproductions on CPython 3.12.3 and 3.13.16 show two causes: unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase instances hold a contextvars.Context, which cannot be pickled, and four dynamically built TestCase classes cannot be found under their qualified names. unittest-parallel 1.8.6 is not adopted.
limitations: Only ubuntu-24.04 ran. The 20 macos-15 jobs never received a runner (zero steps), so this receipt shows nothing about macOS timing, macOS correctness or a macOS verdict.

Every parallel run crashed before its summary. Its seconds cover the tests that ran (9,624 result records in each L4 and L4F run, 9,741 in each L4C run, of 9,823) and the crash, not a complete suite; the serial seconds of the missing tests were not measured. The speed ratios are therefore not a whole-suite speed result.

The speed ratios inside the preregistered bounds (median at most 0.60 of S's median and slowest at most 0.75 of S's fastest) hold for all three parallel arms (L4 0.2767 and 0.5472; L4F 0.4171 and 0.5987; L4C 0.4020 and 0.5936), but no arm is eligible, so they are not an adoption claim.
The serial baseline varied on one runner type and image: S test steps of 1,186 to 1,688 s (jobs of 1,212 to 1,724 s). The cause of that spread is not known.

tests.test_order_throughput.CapacityRunTests.test_cli_refuses_live_base_url_from_env_file_without_network was ERROR in 3 of 3 L4F runs and ok in all S, L4 and L4C runs. Its cause is not known: unittest-parallel prints its error report only after pool.map returns (main.py:193-211 at bda5d77), so the crash suppressed the traceback. The module alone passes locally (Ran 76 tests, OK (skipped=1)) both serially and unpooled under unittest-parallel on CPython 3.12.3 and 3.13.16.

tests.test_secret_path_guard.K4GuardTests.test_k4_timing failed in 3 of 3 L4C runs, on different subtests each time, and passed in all 3 S runs and all 6 module-level runs (L4 and L4F, each with 4 workers). It is the slowest serial test (30.7 to 60.0 s). Whether the class-level failures come from CPU contention alone is not shown.

The hosted logs show only one exception per run, the TypeError, because CPython's MapResult keeps only the first exception of a map (Lib/multiprocessing/pool.py:822 at v3.12.3). The PicklingError of the four dynamic classes in tests/test_adoption_version_probes.py was reproduced locally; its hosted effect is inferred from the missing ids (exactly those four classes at class level).

GitHub's 90-day run retention covers the run and job records, and the 18 artifacts expire on 2026-11-02. The full result.json (815,073 bytes), the raw logs and the two 9,823-id inventories are not published; their sha256 values are kept here with sanitized excerpts and a trimmed oracle output.

The cancellation was the coordinator's decision, not part of the preregistered rule. No macOS job had started, so no macOS attempt was voided or hidden. The macOS queue observation counts this repository's macOS jobs only; other repositories that draw on the same account's macOS concurrency were not read.

Sanitization: runner paths in the retained excerpts became <workspace> and <runner-home>, and local paths in the local reproductions became <venv-3.12.3>, <venv-3.13.16>, <cpython-3.12.3> and <cpython-3.13.16>. summary.md, checkout-status.json and the preregistered experiment record are byte copies.

The preregistration asked for an observed record (native_cli_execution observations) beside its experiment.json. That directory exists only on the unmerged trial branch, so this receipt and its decision record carry the same per-run data instead, and the preregistered experiment record is kept as preregistration-experiment.json.txt so that no validator reads it as a live convergence record.
The local reproductions ran on this worker's WSL2 host in existing virtual environments with unittest-parallel 1.8.6 and coverage 7.16.2 (local integration evidence), not on a hosted runner.

reasons: the failure is deterministic: one exception, at the same line, in 9 of 9 parallel runs, with identical sets of ids that never ran in every run of a level

it does not depend on the platform: IsolatedAsyncioTestCase holds a contextvars.Context on CPython 3.12.3 and 3.13.16 (the macOS arms' line), and pickling looks a class up by its qualified name on every platform; the local reproductions fail the same way on both versions, so every macOS parallel arm would hit the same three modules and macOS could only end in reject or no verdict (an inference, not a macOS run)

the shared macOS pool was held up: five of this repository's macOS jobs held runners in 46 of 50 sampled minutes (macos_queue_observation); had they started, the 20 trial jobs would have held runners while other pull requests' required checks waited

async_test_cases.mechanism: unittest-parallel sends each suite of live TestCase instances to a spawned worker by pickling it; an IsolatedAsyncioTestCase instance holds a contextvars.Context, which cannot be pickled, so a module suite (or, at class level, a class suite) that contains one is never sent and its tests never run
async_test_cases.evidence: hosted: the TypeError ends all nine parallel runs, and at class level exactly FeeSnapshot (7) and AsyncTransport (59) are missing from these two modules; local: a toy module with one plain and one IsolatedAsyncioTestCase class fails at module level and runs only its plain class at class level, and a plain-only module passes, on CPython 3.12.3 and 3.13.16; source: async_case.py and pool.py as cited
